items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Jelly Roll Morton and Mabel ('Jelly Roll took Mabel', 'she met Jelly Roll'), but does not describe a personal relationship with Mabel herself.

ctx.x: A whole (?). "Chinaman and Mabel/Sat down at a table/Down in a cabaret." That's a story of a Chinaman, a nice Chinaman, he's seeing this woman, and he's out with her, and he's gonna make it with her, and then he sees that she's got this ring on her finger. It's a legendary song like "Frankie and Johnny" or "St. James." But it's "The Chinaman and..."

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And the youngest sister, my aunt, we were born the same year, the youngest Barbarin daughter.

ctx.x: Now, you've got Paul Barbarin. Tell us about Paul Barbarin.

Paul Barbarin is my godfather. That's my mother's oldest brother. There's four brothers, and you had four brothers and five sisters. And Paul Barbarin was the oldest brother who was a drummer, and Louis was a drummer, Lucien's a drummer, and Willie's a trumpet player. There was four brothers. Paul coming down two years younger, Louis two years younger, Lucien two years younger, Willie... And then there's a girl stuck there two years younger than Willie. And I am two years younger than Willie. And the youngest…

And from that, you can see the four boys beatin' around the house on drums, and the old man walkin' up and down the house with his mellophone and his baritone horn -- and there was music all the time.
